History:
- Presenting complaint: New swelling of the left elbow noted approximately 1 week ago, first noticed in the shower.
- Onset/duration/progression: Began ~1 week prior; not improving, described as slightly warm and with a fluid-like sensation; no clear progression to date.
- Symptoms/associated features: Minimal pain — can move elbow normally; area adjacent to the swelling feels "weird" and is a bit tender to pressure; tip of elbow not especially tender; skin over tip described as a bit dry. No systemic symptoms reported.
- Triggers/etiology: No antecedent trauma or injury reported. No prior similar episodes.
- Social/functional: Desk job, physically active — runs 2–3 times per week.

Past Medical History:
- Osteoarthritis — diagnosed by GP several years ago.
- Allergies: Peanuts.
- Medication: None routinely taken. (No prescription/OTC meds otherwise documented.)
- No known drug allergies.

Physical Examination:
- Inspection of left elbow: visible swelling over elbow region.
- Local findings: area slightly warmer than adjacent skin; mild tenderness adjacent to swelling on palpation; tip of elbow not markedly tender; skin over tip somewhat dry.
- Function: Full/normal range of motion of the elbow reported by patient and observed.
- Provider assessment: Appearance not consistent with septic arthritis on current exam.
- No other exam findings documented (vital signs, systemic exam not provided).

Impression:
- Left olecranon bursitis (clinical impression of bursitis).

Management Plan:
- Pharmacologic: Advise oral ibuprofen 400 mg, twice daily, to be taken after food; stop if heartburn occurs. (Route not documented.)
- Investigations: Arrange blood tests (forms to be sent to patient's home) — planned full screen including inflammatory markers, infection screen, rheumatologic antibodies, and evaluation for gout.
- Follow-up: Review blood test results when available (results expected in ~5–6 days after test); arrange follow-up appointment (phone/video or face-to-face as needed) to reassess and review results.
- Safety advice/urgent actions: Return or seek immediate review if elbow becomes very red, very painful, or if redness spreads — would require urgent assessment for possible infection.

Patient Summary:
- Patient developed a nontraumatic left elbow swelling ~1 week ago, with minimal pain and slight warmth. Clinician suspects olecranon bursitis and advised an NSAID (ibuprofen) and a blood test screen to evaluate for inflammatory, infectious, rheumatologic, and gout causes; follow-up will occur after results or sooner if symptoms worsen.

Key Takeaways:
- Start ibuprofen 400 mg twice daily after food; stop if heartburn occurs.
- Complete the blood tests when the forms arrive to your home.
- Seek urgent review if the elbow becomes markedly more painful, very red, or the redness spreads.

Next Steps:
- Patient to receive blood test forms by post and to have blood tests performed at specified location per instructions in pack.
- Clinic to review blood results (~5–6 days after blood draw) and arrange follow-up (phone/video or in-person per patient preference).
- Escalate to urgent in-person assessment if signs of local infection develop.

Quality checks:
- Missing but clinically expected elements: vital signs; detailed systemic exam; documentation of neurovascular status of the limb; medication reconciliation (current/PRN/OTC beyond patient statement); route for ibuprofen not explicitly documented; imaging (e.g., ultrasound/x-ray) or aspiration/culture not performed or documented.
- Internal conflicts from transcript: none identified.
- Transcript quality comment: Encounter audio/transcript generally clear; minor conversational pauses and stuttering but clinical details adequately documented.
